new_result.statement: For mutually independent original-coordinate blocks Z,X,Y, rank-two B with singular-product Delta, c in ran B, d in ran B^T, theta=d^T B^+ c, and Q=aZ^2+bZ+2Zc^TX+2Zd^TY+F(X)+G(Y)+2X^TBY, if a!=0 and a!=theta then Q has an absolutely continuous law with ||p_Q||inf <=8 Delta^(-1/4)(|a||a-theta|)^(-1/4). Continuity not claimed.
new_result.proof_key: Complete the original scalar square; B_a=B-cd^T/a. In thin-SVD coordinates det(Sigma-gamma delta^T/a)=Delta(a-theta)/a, so the post-pivot cross block remains rank two with singular-product Delta|a-theta|/|a|. Apply the source-valid rank-two cross half-Riesz endpoint and the conditional square-density formula.

primary_source.authors: Galyna Livshyts; Grigoris Paouris; Peter Pivovarov
primary_source.title: On sharp bounds for marginal densities of product measures
primary_source.used_scope: k=2 orthogonal marginals of original-coordinate cap-one product banks have density cap 2

partner_application: An outer nonzero original scalar pivot r gives ||p||inf <=4sqrt(2)|r|^(-1/2)Delta^(-1/8)(|a||a-theta|)^(-1/8). For Q1=(W+Z)^2+Q0 with Q0=2Z^2+2ZX1+2ZY1+2X1Y1+2X2Y2, the bound is 2^(19/8)=5.187358218604039 and spectrum {4,1,1,-1,-1,0}.
